# Finding ∫ -2·x⁴·sin(x) dx

## Strategy: Integration by Parts (Tabular Method)

First, factor out the constant:
$$\int -2x^4 \sin(x)\, dx = -2\int x^4 \sin(x)\, dx$$

## Tabular Integration by Parts

| Sign | Derivatives of x⁴ | Integrals of sin(x) |
|:----:|:-----------------:|:-------------------:|
| +    | x⁴               | −cos(x)             |
| −    | 4x³              | −sin(x)             |
| +    | 12x²             | cos(x)              |
| −    | 24x              | sin(x)              |
| +    | 24               | −cos(x)             |

**Multiply along diagonals:**

$$\int x^4 \sin(x)\, dx = -x^4\cos(x) + 4x^3\sin(x) + 12x^2\cos(x) - 24x\sin(x) - 24\cos(x)$$

## Multiply by −2

$$-2\left[-x^4\cos(x) + 4x^3\sin(x) + 12x^2\cos(x) - 24x\sin(x) - 24\cos(x)\right]$$

$$= 2x^4\cos(x) - 8x^3\sin(x) - 24x^2\cos(x) + 48x\sin(x) + 48\cos(x)$$

## Verification (differentiate the result)

- d/dx[2x⁴cos(x)] = 8x³cos(x) − 2x⁴sin(x)
- d/dx[−8x³sin(x)] = −24x²sin(x) − 8x³cos(x)
- d/dx[−24x²cos(x)] = −48xcos(x) + 24x²sin(x)
- d/dx[48xsin(x)] = 48sin(x) + 48xcos(x)
- d/dx[48cos(x)] = −48sin(x)

All intermediate terms cancel, leaving **−2x⁴sin(x)** ✓

<answer>2*x**4*cos(x) - 8*x**3*sin(x) - 24*x**2*cos(x) + 48*x*sin(x) + 48*cos(x) + C</answer>
